reviewBoundary: New complete junior and senior text practices. Every question has a material evidence quote, explicit key and candidate/form review; completion limits are visible. units.title: 高一专项：安静休息室与自行车检查

materials.title: A Room to Pause
materials.text:
A student festival can be enjoyable and tiring at the same time. Our organising team decided to offer a quiet room where visitors could sit away from the main activities. The first question was what the room was for. ____1____ It was not another performance space or a place where visitors would be asked to join a group game.

We described its purpose on the event map, but that was not enough. People also needed to find it from the busy entrance. ____2____ A small sign hidden behind a stall would not help someone who had already decided to take a break.

Inside, we provided ordinary chairs and left clear paths between them. We avoided arranging every seat in a circle. ____3____ A person could sit on their own without appearing to leave an activity that everyone else was doing.

Volunteers at the door were asked to explain the room briefly and then give visitors space. ____4____ Someone who wanted company could ask, while someone who preferred silence would not have to refuse repeated conversation.

Before the festival opened, several students tried walking from the entrance to the room and back. ____5____ One noticed that a sign pointed towards a locked corridor. We corrected it before visitors arrived and kept a volunteer nearby in case anybody still needed directions.

Every visitor had to tell the group why they needed a break.
A friendly welcome did not need to become a continuous conversation.

materials.title: Before the Bicycle Leaves
materials.text:
Last Saturday, our cycling club invited a mechanic to demonstrate a simple bicycle check. He ____1____ (BEGIN) by asking us to look at the tyres before touching the tools. Each bicycle was held steady ____2____ a volunteer while its owner watched.

The mechanic showed us a brake cable ____3____ had become loose. He did not ask us to ride the bicycle to test it. Instead, he explained ____4____ the brake should be checked before anyone set off.

I had brought the bicycle that my sister no longer used. Its saddle was ____5____ (HIGH) than I needed, so the mechanic adjusted it for me. He asked me ____6____ (SIT) on it while another adult kept the bicycle still.

After ____7____ (WATCH) the demonstration, we wrote down the order of the checks. The mechanic said that recognising a problem was not the same as knowing how ____8____ (REPAIR) it. If we were unsure, we should ask someone qualified to help.

At the end, we returned the borrowed tools to ____9____ (THEY) box. The session had made me more ____10____ (CARE) about preparing for a ride, not more willing to ignore a fault.

units.title: 高二专项：教室声音与包裹时刻表

materials.title: What Did the Reading Measure?
materials.text:
Two classrooms seemed to sound different during group work, so a science club planned a small comparison. Before choosing equipment, the members had to say what they wanted to compare. ____1____ The loudest instant, the average level over a minute and how clearly a voice could be heard were different questions.

They decided to compare an average reading during a short, repeated activity. The measuring device would stand in the same relative position in each room. ____2____ Placing it next to a talking pupil in one room and beside an empty wall in the other would make the readings difficult to interpret.

The club also noted how many pupils took part and what they were asked to do. ____3____ A reading from silent individual work could not fairly stand in for the sound of a lively discussion, even if both took place in the same classroom.

One pupil wanted to announce that the room with the lower reading was better for learning. The teacher asked the club to slow down. ____4____ A quieter measurement alone did not show whether everyone had heard the instructions or understood the task.

The final report described the equipment, positions and activity before presenting the numbers. ____5____ Another class could then decide whether repeating the comparison would answer a useful question of its own. The club had measured one defined feature of two situations, rather than ranked every possible use of the rooms.

Otherwise, location might explain a difference attributed to the rooms.

materials.title: The Timetable for Parcels
materials.text:
The timetable we found in a box of station papers was not the one we had expected. Instead of listing passenger departures, it recorded when parcels ____1____ (COLLECT) from nearby villages. The heading, ____2____ was partly hidden by a stain, had led us to misread its purpose.

Once the paper had been examined under better light, the archivist asked us ____3____ (COMPARE) it with a delivery book from the same year. Several place names appeared in both, but their order was different. We needed to discover ____4____ the two lists described the same journey or separate ones.

A note beside one village gave an ____5____ (EXPLAIN). The road had been closed for repairs, so parcels from that area had reached the station by another route. Without ____6____ (NOTICE) the note, we might have treated the changed order as a copying mistake.

The discovery did not answer every question. No departure time ____7____ (GIVE) for the return journey, and the book did not identify the person ____8____ had written the note. We recorded those gaps rather than inventing missing details.

Our final description was more ____9____ (ACCURACY) than the label we had drafted at first. It explained not only what the timetable contained, but also why an initial reading had made ____10____ (WE) think it was a passenger service.

units.title: 高三专项：会议材料与复原溪流观察

materials.title: What the Meeting Papers Can Say
materials.text:
Two accounts of the same committee meeting can disagree without either writer having invented the whole event. One may record decisions; the other may preserve discussion. ____1____ Before treating a difference as a contradiction, ask what each document was intended to do.

The distinction becomes important when a proposal appears in one account but not the other. A discussion note may record an idea that never reached a vote. ____2____ Its absence from a list of final decisions would then be expected rather than suspicious.

Direct speech presents another difficulty. A polished sentence in a later summary may not reproduce the words spoken in the room. ____3____ The wording can still communicate the writer's understanding, but it should not automatically be presented as a verbatim quotation.

When possible, compare both accounts with materials whose timing is clear. An agenda circulated before the meeting may establish that a subject was planned for discussion. ____4____ It cannot, on its own, prove what the participants eventually agreed to do.

A responsible reconstruction therefore keeps several categories visible: planned topics, reported remarks and recorded decisions. ____5____ Readers can then follow the interpretation while seeing where the surviving papers leave a question open. Clarity comes from showing the path through the evidence, not from forcing the papers to tell a perfectly smooth story.

materials.title: Returning to the Restored Stream
materials.text:
Only after we had visited the restored stream in different seasons ____1____ (WE/BEGIN) to understand the limits of our first photographs. The bright summer images had made the banks look completely bare, ____2____ some of the plants were simply dormant at that time.

The ecologist ____3____ (LEAD) the survey asked us to mark the same short sections on every visit. Otherwise, a change in where we stood might be mistaken ____4____ a change in the stream itself. She also reminded us that a photograph could not show everything happening below the surface.

Several small barriers ____5____ (REMOVE) before the survey started. That did not mean every later difference could automatically be attributed to their removal. Weather, maintenance and activity upstream all needed ____6____ (CONSIDER).

What interested me most ____7____ (BE) the difference between a promise in the project leaflet and a question in the survey notebook. The leaflet described what the work hoped to achieve; the notebook recorded ____8____ those hopes were supported by observations at particular places and times.

Had we relied on the first visit alone, we ____9____ (MISS) some of that variation. Repeated visits did not remove all uncertainty, but they made the ____10____ (RELATION) between claims and observations easier to discuss.

units.title: 初一阅读：模型火车展的参观安排

materials.title: A Ticket for the Train Show
materials.text:
Tom is taking his little brother to a model-train show on Saturday. Their tickets are for the ten o'clock visit. The hall opens at nine thirty, but the first train demonstration does not start until ten fifteen. Tom wants to see it, so they will stay after entering.

The hall has two doors. Visitors with tickets use the side door. The front door is for the people who bring the train models. There is a small bag table beside the side door, where a volunteer can look inside visitors' bags.

Tom's brother wants to bring his new toy train. Tom reads the ticket again. It says visitors may carry a toy, but they must keep it in a bag inside the hall. Only the display models can run on the tracks. Tom puts a notebook in his bag too. His brother can draw his favourite train and ask about its colours instead of putting his own train on a track.

At eleven, the brothers will meet their aunt at the café across the street. They will leave the hall through the side door and cross at the traffic lights.

units.title: 初一阅读：豆种交换桌的收尾

materials.title: One Seed for a Small Pot
materials.text:
The school garden has a small seed table today. Ava brings three paper bags of bean seeds from home. The teacher checks the bags and asks her to put one on the table. The other two will stay in the garden cupboard for next week's class.

Each visitor can take one seed from the table. Beside the seeds, Ava places some small empty pots and a bowl of dry soil. The pots are free, but visitors must fill them at the table. They should not take the whole bowl away.

Ben comes with his own pot. It already has soil in it, so he only needs a seed. Ava shows him the picture on the bag. It says beans need a place with light. Ben decides to keep his pot by the kitchen window. He will not leave it in the dark cupboard under the stairs.

At the end of the afternoon, Ava puts the unused pots back in a box. The teacher carries the soil to the garden. Ava wipes the table with a cloth before returning to her classroom.

units.title: 初二阅读：为家庭观众挑选短片

materials.title: A Film for This Audience
materials.text:
A local cinema invited our school to help choose a short film for a family afternoon. Three pupils, including me, joined the selection group. At first, we wanted to vote for the film that had made us laugh most. The cinema manager asked us to think about the audience before voting.

The programme would include younger children who were still learning to read. One funny film used long written messages to explain nearly every action. Another had fewer words but depended on a joke about a television show that none of the youngest visitors would know. The manager did not say that either film was bad. She said that a choice for this afternoon needed a reason connected with its audience.

We watched the third film again. Its story followed a child trying to return a lost glove. We could understand the main events from actions, though there were a few spoken lines. The ending also gave families something simple to talk about afterwards: why the child had helped a stranger.

We selected it and wrote a short explanation of our decision. On the day, the manager asked families for comments after the screening. Some parents liked being able to discuss the story with their children. One child said that the last scene was too quick. We kept that comment too, because choosing a film did not mean refusing to hear what could have worked better.

questions.prompt: What did the pupils initially want to base their vote on?
options: Which film had made them laugh most.
Which film had the longest written messages.
Which film was the manager’s favourite.
Which film had already won a school prize.
questions.explanation: A正确：at first按笑得最多投票；B字长非初衷；C未按经理最爱；D无奖项信息。

questions.prompt: Why might the first funny film be difficult for some visitors?
options: It had no clear ending at all.
It relied heavily on reading long messages.
It was about a lost glove.
It was shown without pictures.
questions.explanation: B正确：年幼儿童识字仍在学，片靠长文字；A结尾未说无；C是第三片；D并非无画面。

questions.prompt: What was useful about the third film’s main events?

They were explained only in a printed booklet.
They could be understood mainly from actions.
They changed every time the group watched.
questions.explanation: C正确：主事件从动作理解；A是第二片问题；B无小册；D未变剧情。

questions.prompt: What could families discuss after the chosen film?
options: How to make a long cinema timetable.
Which television programme was most popular.
Why cinemas should stop showing short films.
Why the child helped a stranger.
questions.explanation: D正确：第三片结局便于谈助陌生人动机；A、B不是此讨论点；C不涉及停播。

questions.prompt: Why was the child’s critical comment kept?
options: Selecting a film did not mean ignoring suggestions for improvement.
The group wanted to cancel every future screening.
It proved that nobody understood the film.
The manager required every ending to be slower.
questions.explanation: A正确：选中不等拒听可改善处；B无取消；C一人觉得末幕快不等无人懂；D无所有片慢结尾规定。

units.title: 初二完形：攀爬前先学会下来

materials.title: The Way Back to the Floor
materials.text:
On our first day at the climbing centre, I thought the hardest part would be reaching the top. The instructor started with something much ____1____: learning to come down. We practised close to the floor, with staff checking the safety system.

I was impatient. My friend had already climbed before, and I wanted to show that I could do ____2____ too. When the instructor asked us to explain the return steps, I could not remember the first one. Instead of laughing, my friend ____3____ to watch me practise it again.

This time, I paid attention to the order. I asked a question whenever I was ____4____ about what to do next. The instructor said that asking at that stage was more useful than making a guess later, when I might be tired.

When it was my turn to climb, I did not reach the highest hold. I stopped where I still felt ready to follow the steps for coming down. My friend waited until I was safely on the floor before ____5____ me about the route.

On the bus home, I said that I had expected the day to be about height. My friend pointed ____6____ that I had learned another skill: knowing when to ask and when to stop. I wrote the return steps in my notebook so that I could read them at home ____7____ our next supervised session, rather than first seeing them during it. The page did not replace an instructor, but it helped me remember ____8____ I needed to practise.

options: lower
older
slower
louder
questions.explanation: A正确：先学靠地面的下降，much lower与登顶对比；B年龄、C速度、D音量非高度对比。

options: it
them
these
those
questions.explanation: A正确：it指climbed这项活动，do it too；B/C/D复数指代不合此动作。

options: forgot
offered
refused
pretended
questions.explanation: B正确：朋友友好主动offer to watch；A忘了不合再练陪看；C拒绝相反；D假装无此意。

options: certain
famous
unsure
pleased
questions.explanation: C正确：不确定下一步才问；A确定相反；B名气无关；D高兴非疑惑。

options: shouting
hiding
leaving
asking
questions.explanation: D正确：安全回地后问路线；A喊她、B藏她、C离开她不构成talk about route情境。

options: out
in
on
away
questions.explanation: A正确：pointed out that指出；B/C/D不构成该短语动词。

options: during
before
between
except
questions.explanation: B正确：at home及rather than during it明确在下次课程前复习；A与该对照矛盾；C缺between两项；D排除非时间先后。

options: who
whose
what
where
questions.explanation: C正确：what作needed to practise宾语；A who人物、B whose所属、D where地点均不合所需步骤技能。

units.title: 初二语法：步行导览中的店铺录音

materials.title: The Version Visitors Will Hear
materials.text:
Our class helped to record stories for a town walking route last week. The teacher ____1____ (ASK) us to work in pairs. Each pair chose one building and prepared questions about ____2____ (IT) history.

My partner and I visited a shop ____3____ had once sold shoes. Its owner showed us an old photograph. The front of the building looked ____4____ (DIFFERENT) from the street view we knew, but the name above the door was the same.

Before ____5____ (RECORD) his story, we explained where the sound file would be used. He agreed to take part but asked us not to include his home address. We wrote that request down ____6____ (CAREFUL).

Back at school, we listened to the file and checked the place names. The recording was longer ____7____ the route needed, so we asked the owner to approve a shorter version. We did not simply remove sentences and assume that the meaning stayed the same.

Next week, we plan ____8____ (SEND) him the final file. His story will help visitors understand one building, and he will know exactly which version they can hear.

questions.explanation: last week过去asked谓语。
history前用物主its，不用it is缩写。
shop在关系从句作sold主语，which/that；where只能地点状语。
look系动词后形容词different，from固定比较。
Before介词后recording动名词。
修饰wrote down用副词carefully。
longer than比较结构，then表示然后不合。
plan to do不定式to send。

units.title: 初三阅读：纸树雕塑如何穿过转角

materials.title: More than the Width of a Door
materials.text:
Our school art club was invited to display work at a community centre. We planned to take a large paper sculpture that looked like a tree. In the art room it stood comfortably beside the windows, but that did not tell us whether it would fit through every doorway on the journey.

The centre sent us the size of its main entrance. At first, we checked only that measurement. Then a caretaker asked about the narrow turn between the entrance and the exhibition room. The sculpture could fit through the outer door and still become impossible to turn inside. We asked for a sketch of the route and measured the model at its widest points.

One member suggested bending the branches to make the sculpture smaller. The student who had made it explained that several paper joints might tear. Instead, we tested whether two sections could be separated at the original connecting points. This worked without changing the shape, and the maker showed two members how to join them again.

We labelled the sections and carried them in separate boxes. At the centre, we assembled the tree in the exhibition room, then took the empty boxes out of the visitors' path. The sculpture arrived safely because we had checked the whole route and asked the maker about its construction, not because one door happened to be large enough.

questions.prompt: What did the sculpture’s position in the art room fail to show?
options: Whether it could pass every part of the delivery route.
Whether it had been made from paper.
Whether the club wanted to display it.
Whether it stood near a window.
questions.explanation: A正确：原教室放得下不证路程门道都可过；B材料已知；C邀请后计划明确；D窗旁位置明确。

questions.prompt: What extra difficulty did the caretaker identify?
options: The centre had no main entrance.
A narrow turn after the entrance.
The art room had been locked.
The sculpture was shorter than the boxes.
questions.explanation: B正确：门后窄转角；A入口存在；C非锁门；D未比较箱高。

questions.prompt: Why was bending the branches rejected?
options: It would change the colour of the paint.
No one could find the maker.
Some paper joints might tear.
The centre wanted only metal sculptures.
questions.explanation: C正确：纸关节可能撕裂；A颜色无此因果；B作者现场解释；D不要求金属。

options: Every branch was cut off permanently.
The caretaker bought a new sculpture.
The boxes were left in the entrance.
The maker taught two members how to reconnect the sections.
questions.explanation: D正确：作者教两人重新接；A非永久剪枝；B未买新；C箱子移出通道。

questions.prompt: What was the main lesson of the delivery?
options: Check the complete route and understand how the object is built.
Only measure the largest door.
Always bend fragile parts without asking.
Keep empty boxes where visitors need to walk.
questions.explanation: A正确：结尾全路线与问作者构造；B是初始不足；C有撕裂风险；D与清通道相反。

units.title: 初三完形：问题下面留出的空白

materials.title: A Space for the Next Question
materials.text:
I used to think that a good interview was one in which the guest answered every question quickly. When our history teacher asked us to interview an older neighbour, I prepared a long list and imagined finishing it in twenty minutes. My neighbour, Mrs Lin, did not follow my ____1____.

I asked when she had first moved to our street. She looked out of the window and was silent. I almost asked the next question, but then I ____2____ that silence might mean she was remembering. After a while, she described carrying a small blue suitcase past the bakery.

The suitcase was not on my list. I asked ____3____ it had been important to her. She said it held the first things she had bought with money she had earned herself. That answer helped me understand the move ____4____ than a date alone could have done.

Later, she mentioned a shop that no longer existed. Although I had never seen the shop, I did not ____5____ to know where it had been. I asked her to describe the buildings beside it. We compared her memory with a street plan only after she had finished the story.

Before leaving, I showed her my notes. One sentence had made her sound ____6____ about a change that she had actually welcomed. She corrected it, and I crossed out my version rather than arguing that I had written it down.

At school, I still reported the main dates, but I also explained how my questions had ____7____ during the conversation. I had not completed every item on the list. ____8____, I had learned why some unexpected details mattered. The teacher said that a list could guide an interview without ____9____ it. I now leave space beneath my questions, ____10____ for an answer but also for a question I have not thought of yet.

options: plan
window
suitcase
bakery
questions.explanation: A正确：访谈未按预备列表计划走；B窗、C箱、D店均非被遵循安排。

options: forgot
realised
complained
ordered
questions.explanation: B正确：意识到沉默可能回忆；A忘记相反；C抱怨、D命令不符合反思。

options: where
when
why
whose
questions.explanation: C正确：问箱为何重要，后答自挣买物意义；A地、B时、D所属非该答。

options: less
later
slower
better
questions.explanation: D正确：个人意义帮助更好理解搬家；A更少相反；B较晚、C慢非理解程度。

options: pretend
repair
deliver
lend
questions.explanation: A正确：虽从没见过不装知道，用pretend to know；B repair修理、C deliver递送、D lend借出均不能在此接to know表示装作知道。

options: pleased
unhappy
careful
certain
questions.explanation: B正确：误记使她像不满，而实际欢迎，unhappy与welcomed对照；A开心不构成误记反差；C谨慎、D确定无此信息。

options: disappeared
stopped
changed
returned
questions.explanation: C正确：新增箱问题显示问题调整；A没全消失；B会话未止；D无回原题描述。

options: Whenever
Until
Unless
Instead
questions.explanation: D正确：未完成每题，取而代之学到意外细节意义；A whenever、B until、C unless都是从属连接词，此处独立句前不构成所需连句副词。

options: controlling
joining
hearing
opening
questions.explanation: A正确：列表可引导却不控制访谈；B joining加入、C hearing听、D opening开始均非与guide对照的完全主导含义。

options: only
not only
no longer
as soon
questions.explanation: B正确：not only...but also并列答案与新问题；A only排他不合but also；C不再、D一就均不成结构。

units.title: 初三对话：地图标题应由谁来写

materials.title: Before the Map Goes on the Wall
materials.text:
Nina and Owen are planning a class display of hand-made maps. Nina has collected the drawings, but one map has no title. They discuss what to do before putting it on the wall.

Nina: This map is beautiful, but I cannot tell which part of town it shows.
Owen: ____1____
Nina: I checked the back. There is only a name: Farah.
Owen: ____2____
Nina: She is at music practice now. We can ask her after lunch.
Owen: ____3____
Nina: Good idea. We can prepare the space and leave a small note where her map will go.
Owen: ____4____
Nina: No, I would rather let her choose the title. We might describe the wrong place.
Owen: ____5____
Nina: Yes. A caption in her own words will help people understand why she chose those streets.

questions.prompt: Gap 1: Choose one sentence from the shared candidates.
options: Should we invent a title for it ourselves?
I cannot come to music practice yesterday.
Could we ask Farah which area it represents?
We can ask her to write a short caption as well.
Have you looked on the back for any information?
We should throw away every map that has a title.
Then let us put up the other maps while we wait.
questions.explanation: E正确：look back引出下一句已查背面；C问作者应先知名字后；G布置其他需等待计划；A拟题后段；D说明文字末段；F扔有题图荒谬；B时态不合且无关。

questions.prompt: Gap 2: Choose one sentence from the shared candidates.
options: Should we invent a title for it ourselves?
I cannot come to music practice yesterday.
Could we ask Farah which area it represents?
We can ask her to write a short caption as well.
Have you looked on the back for any information?
We should throw away every map that has a title.
Then let us put up the other maps while we wait.
questions.explanation: C正确：已知Farah姓名后建议问她，下一句答她在练音乐午后能问；E背面已查；G等待布置下一空；A拟题会引No回应而此处答时间；D未谈caption；F、B不合。

questions.prompt: Gap 3: Choose one sentence from the shared candidates.
options: Should we invent a title for it ourselves?
I cannot come to music practice yesterday.
Could we ask Farah which area it represents?
We can ask her to write a short caption as well.
Have you looked on the back for any information?
We should throw away every map that has a title.
Then let us put up the other maps while we wait.
questions.explanation: G正确：等午后先放其他地图，下一句Good idea准备空位；E重复背面，C刚约午后，A拟题应接拒绝，D写caption需作者在场，F和B不合。

questions.prompt: Gap 4: Choose one sentence from the shared candidates.
options: Should we invent a title for it ourselves?
I cannot come to music practice yesterday.
Could we ask Farah which area it represents?
We can ask her to write a short caption as well.
Have you looked on the back for any information?
We should throw away every map that has a title.
Then let us put up the other maps while we wait.
questions.explanation: A正确：Should we自己拟题对应No,I would rather let her choose；E背面无须拒偏好；C问Farah会获同意而非No；G放别图已同意；D写caption末句Yes；F不符任务，B句意时态错。

questions.prompt: Gap 5: Choose one sentence from the shared candidates.
options: Should we invent a title for it ourselves?
I cannot come to music practice yesterday.
Could we ask Farah which area it represents?
We can ask her to write a short caption as well.
Have you looked on the back for any information?
We should throw away every map that has a title.
Then let us put up the other maps while we wait.
questions.explanation: D正确：caption建议对应Yes,E caption in her own words；E背面、C区域问题不直接指caption，G布置已定，A拟题已拒，F毁图、B时态混乱均非收尾建议。
